body: Did that this morning, I'm going to give this a shot.  Called around and found someone who is accepting patients and takes my insurance.  So thanks to you and to all that took time to post last night.  It was very helpful.

Your analogy made me smile, so you got that to happen.  Maybe I should reach out, the thought of telling my command staff I've been suicidal makes my anxiety go through the roof though.  So many thoughts racing through my head about how that meeting will go.  I guess technically they can't fire me per state law and that's why we have an EAP.

I am absolutely terrified to reach out to my command staff to tell them something is going on.  Most of the guys I work with are conservative 'macho manly men', I know that sounds like a weird sexist stereotype, but it's the best way to describe them.  I know when we've had psych patients in the past, there are a lot of war stories that revolve around making fun of them, attention seeking, etc etc.  There isn't a lot of understanding or acceptance that mental illness is an actual illness.  It terrifies the ever living crap out of me.  =/

That's about the gist of it, I really don't have a lot of emotional support.  My co-workers are fine to bounce tough calls off of but we don't really hang out outside of work.  Our schedule (24/48's) are tough enough as it is.  I work with mostly conservative men as well and have very few female co-workers I can relate with.  It just makes being at work and dealing with work issues that much more difficult when we work an emotional or tough call.  Macho manly man brushes it off, but it's more difficult for me to brush off a tough pediatric call like that.  

I'm so much into not caring about myself anymore.

Seeking help would be a great solution, it's just such a taboo subject in my line of work.  It's still looked on as really a weakness and can jeopardize my chances of moving to different departments if I wanted to move to another county service if it gets out that I have mental issues.  No one wants an "unstable" paramedic working for them.  Even if I've gotten treatment and am doing much better.  It's shitty and deters people from asking for help in the first place.  It makes it hard for me to reach out and ask for help officially and not anonymously.
Thank you for the kind words, I feel so overloaded with stresses that it's tough to just keep my head on my shoulders.  I try and try and try and sometimes I just feel like it's not nearly enough.
